title: Chapter 1033 The Last Judgment
content:
Chapter 1033 The Last Judgment

"Those who choose to go west will no longer have their home in the rear."

"And in front!"

Xi firmly remembers what Li Xin said to him more than two years ago, standing under the snow-capped green hills.

For Li Xin, home is on the other side of the snow-capped mountains, in those lands and cities that have not yet been explored and conquered, at the end of the horseshoe!

Li Xin is like an arrow that Emperor Qin Shi Huang shot in his last life, carrying his last wish. Once he leaves the arrow, he will not look back until he reaches the end! Even Hu Hai's edict and even death could not take away Li Xin's loyalty to the First Emperor!

So a total of 8,000 people headed west. Most of them were young and free-spirited people, good family members and bad boys. They followed Li Xin's footsteps and did not hesitate to wonder what they would do when they went to another world. Joy cannot be known.

But for most people in the expeditionary force, home is still in the east. In the Central Plains there are pines and cypresses tombs of their ancestors, their wives and children looking out in front of the village gate day after day, familiar clothes and local accents, and grain soup that makes people feel at ease.

So under the leadership of Xi and others, more than 10,000 expeditionary troops began their journey back east, and returned to Dunhuang, Zhangye County in March of the "40th year of Qin Shihuang", which was the "first year of the Regency" in their own chronology.

When they entered Yumen Pass, their number had been reduced by half. Thousands of them fell dead on the dry Gobi. Others stayed in the oasis country in the desert and gave up hope of returning home...

Because home is too far away, even if Xi and others reach Dunhuang and see the prefecture and county buildings of Qin again, they are still half the distance from Guanzhong.

Fortunately, the Dang River flowing through Dunhuang nourished the thirsty Western Expeditionary Army. Mingsha Mountain was nothing compared to the great deserts of the Western Regions.

They regrouped in Dunhuang and began to open up the Hexi Corridor from the west. They defeated the Yuezhi princes who tried to return to this fertile land and defended the new territory of Qin.

This delayed them for a long time, and they did not set off again until the spring of the second year of the Regency.

The journey ahead is still long.

The Black Mountain Canyon rises from the Jiuquan rocks.

To the colorful Danxia wonders near Zhangye, the road they walked on their westward journey required the army to re-measure it with their footsteps.

As long as you are still in the Hexi Corridor, on this long road that stretches for thousands of miles, you can see the endless Qilian Mountains in the southwest, seemingly endless, firmly occupying the skyline.

No wonder it was called "Heaven" by the Yuezhi and the Huns.

Looking at the snow on the Qilian Mountains, Xi also touched his bun.

The thin old official who was sent to the Western Regions many years ago had black hair, but now it is gradually turning frosty.

As they walked eastward, the soldiers did not know how many pairs of shoes were worn out. The Hexi Corridor became narrower and narrower, and it seemed to have reached an end. However, if the Western Expeditionary Army wanted to go home, they had to pass the last hurdle: the always dangerous Wusheath. ridge.

There are tall snow-capped mountains on both sides that are covered with snow all year round. The cold air often invades Wushaoling, forming a severe cold air belt standing on the east and west walls. Snow falls in spring and the cold air bites the bones. The Western Expeditionary Army helped each other climb and endured the sudden changes in climate. It took a lot of coldness to overcome this natural danger.

After crossing Wushaoling and Lingju County, at the crossing of Dahe River, Xi met Qiang Hua, the new governor of Zhangye County, and from his mouth, Xi basically learned about the divisions and reunions of the world in recent years.

Qianghua praised Heifu for overcoming the chaos and reunifying the world, but he was happy but did not comment. The Western Expeditionary Army was large in number, and crossing the river was slow, and the march was also slow. However, he received a special permission to take the fastest post to Xianyang. .

"Xia Gong is looking forward to seeing Mr. Xi again day and night, and treating him with high titles and important positions." Qiang Hua said.

But Xi was unmoved and flatly refused.

"I am the supervisor."

"I preach military laws to soldiers all day long, how can I leave the army and leave my post without permission?"

If Xi had not tried his best to control it along the way, this Western Expeditionary Army would have fallen apart countless times, or become a bandit due to hunger and cold.

Xi decided to take care of them to the end, from beginning to end, without making any mistakes.

They crossed the river, entered the Great Wall at Linzhao, followed the route taken by Emperor Qin Shi Huang during his return tour to the west, passed through Longban, and arrived at Guanzhong...

At this point, we have arrived home, and the scenery has become different. There are no large tracts of wilderness, and there are more farmland connected by roads. Under the Zhouyuan Qishan Mountains, men farm and women weave, a peaceful scene that makes people feel uncomfortable. Imagine, this was a battlefield two years ago.

Most of the Western Expeditionary Army was left to eat in Yongdi, waiting for orders to be restored and sent back to their place of origin. Xi also bid farewell to the soldiers who had been with them day and night for three years, and continued to march eastward.

When leaving Yongdi, Xi's carriage carried several newly revised Qin laws. While resting along the way, Xi frowned and looked at them one by one. He wanted to know what gains and losses the laws had made in the past few years.

At nightfall, the pavilion chief knew his identity and offered to add lamps and provide fish, meat, etc., but Xi refused.

"After I resigned as the supervisor of the Western Expeditionary Army, I was just a criminal who was demoted to a superior by the First Emperor of Qin. It is said in "The Law of Chuanshi" that anyone who stays in a pavilion will not go down to seek people or make rice. One bucket, half a liter of sauce, one liter of vegetable soup, half a stone of grass to feed the horses, and no lights or candles are allowed at night. Since this law has not changed, don't treat me specially."

After Heifu captured Xianyang, he sent a document to the northwest to restore Xi Zai's status as an official in the court. However, when Xi saw the document in Dunhuang, he did not accept it.

Xi did not think that the edict was legal and valid at the time, and because of the discrepancy between the information on both sides, the matter went unsolved.

So the stubborn Xi could only read and copy the laws and regulations during the day. When his eyes were dazzled, he walked to the field ridges in the villages along the way, said hello to the farmers and vendors, and asked about the government's recent policies.

Just like a magistrate who is about to handle a major case and conduct a trial, he silently remembers everything he sees and hears, and uses them as evidence in court...

On July 20th of the second year of the Regency, Xi, who had been traveling for a long time, was about to arrive at Duting, ten miles west of Xianyang.

But at this moment, his carriage was stopped by someone!

The servant who was driving the carriage did not recognize the person in front of him. When he saw him stretching out his arms to stop the carriage, he quickly pulled the reins. The carriage stopped more than ten feet away in front of him. Because this trip was of great importance, he couldn't help being nervous and scolded:

"Who are you? Do you know who is in the car? How dare you block it?"

"I know."

The voice was as sonorous and powerful as before.

Even though he had his eyes closed in the car, he couldn't help but open them. His fingertips holding the book were trembling slightly.

"The person sitting in the car is the world-famous Xijun."

"Xijun has been an official for decades. He has fulfilled his duties and is familiar with the laws and regulations. He has served hundreds of prison sentences. There is absolutely no unjust, false or wrong case in his hands. Every one of them has achieved justice according to the laws and regulations."

"His Majesty is cold on the face, but in fact he cares about the people. He even dared to question the First Emperor in court. Now that his injustice has been avenged, he has returned from his journey to the west. As a junior fellow countryman, I am here to welcome you."

The bamboo curtain of the carriage slowly opened, and Xi poked his head out. He was already full of gray hair and weathered by the wind and sand outside the Great Wall. The old official squinted and recognized the identity of the visitor.

The person in front of me is no longer the young young man who stopped a car and complained about injustice in the Huyang Pavilion of Anlu.

He was dressed in regular clothes, with a crown and dark clothes, a thick sagittal beard on his lips, and a sword at his waist. He stood in the middle of the dusty road, folded his hands, and bowed to the emperor.

Only the face, as dark as Guizhou's head, still had a smile.

"Xijun, are you alright?"

…

Xi and Heifu were sitting opposite each other in Du Pavilion.

I vaguely remember that twenty years ago, they first met in an inconspicuous little pavilion in Anlu County.

It's just that the fate of the two people was different. They were both stirred by the wave of this era and deviated from their original trajectories. It was just that Heifu finally became a trend-setter, while Xi Ze drifted further and became more like a witness... …

Witnessed the growth of a little man from a mere head of Guizhou to the true ruler of the empire.

I have also witnessed the ups and downs of an era, with intense ambition and becoming dull...

Xi looked to the side. Legend has it that the stone pier where Bai Qi committed suicide was splashing red. It was here that Xi was demoted to the west by the First Emperor. When he was about to embark on the long road to exile, he passed by Duting.

Because Fusu was the first to plead for Xi and was reprimanded, no one in the civil or military court dared to say goodbye. Only Heihu's wife, Ye, rode a bicycle and gave each other wine. He also gave a house of people for Xi to call his servants and a maid for Xi to wash and prepare meals along the way.

For this reason, Xi specially bowed to Mr. Hei:

"Without this pair of servants to take care of me all the way, I'm afraid I wouldn't be able to survive Li Xina. Thank you Madam Regent. When I went to the Western Regions, they stayed in Dunhuang. Now there are two, two and one girls. If they don't want to return east, I'm afraid I won't be able to bring them back." Returned to the regent’s wife…”

"In addition, I would also like to express my gratitude to the regent for sending someone to Hexi for his kind words."

Heifu returns the courtesy and treats the person he respects with respect, no matter what position he reaches, he will remain as respectful as before:

"Don't worry about the unknown. No one in the world knows you. General Li did know Xijun, and Xijun did not betray the trust of him and the other soldiers. He brought back the people from the Western Expedition safely, and never offended the people along the way. The conflict is extremely difficult."

Xi said: "General Li also knows the regent well. Before he crossed Congling, he asked me to bring you a message."

"What words?"

"General Lee just wanted to ask."

Xi raised his head and looked at Hei Fu:

"Heifu, do you still remember the First Emperor's ambition?"

"The ambition of the First Emperor..."

Heifu was silent for a long time and sighed: "It's clear that the seals are carved on the stones of Hengshan, Zhifu, Jieshi and Langya!"

He stood up and recited those dreams that seemed like those from the previous era.

"Within **, there is the land of the emperor. It stretches across the quicksand in the west, ends in the north in the south. There is the East China Sea in the east, and Daxia in the north. Wherever human beings go, there are all those who do not fail to serve."

"This is the great ambition of the First Emperor to expand the territory of China. It is a pity that the world cannot afford so many conquests. However, it is gratifying that Li Xin can inherit this ambition and lead the army to the west to look after the First Emperor who is sleeping in Lishan Mountain. In the outside world, look at other civilizations outside of Kyushu. With Li Xin’s ability, maybe he can really conquer a mountain and river and spread the reputation of the First Emperor to the country in the far west?"

"This legacy of opening up new territories has been succeeded by Li Xin."

Xi nodded and agreed. Li Xin indeed thought so.

"Also, the First Emperor made people not judge themselves by their posthumous titles, but by counting their descendants. The second and third generations will be passed down to all generations and be passed down to infinity. He hoped that the Qin Dynasty would be prosperous and prosperous forever, and that it would last forever."

"But there is no immortal dynasty in this world. This is true for Xia, Shang and Zhou, so how can Qin be an exception? Although I have supported this crumbling society, everything will remain unknown after my death."

"However, Gongsun Jun, the son of Fusu, has been sealed in Haidong and lives in a corner. As long as there are not too many changes, he may really be able to stay in that country forever and be a part of his family forever."

"Therefore, this legacy of a long lineage may be succeeded by Haidong Hou, just like the Yin Shang Dynasty died, but the Song Dynasty inherited the surname Sheji."

Regarding this, Xi frowned and was noncommittal.

"The First Emperor also promised that the terrain is established, the common people are free from Yao, and the world is well cared for. Men enjoy their fields, women cultivate their careers, and everything is in order. Hui is benefited from all properties, and they come to the fields for a long time. No one is uneasy. Keep things in order. With time, all products will multiply. Guizhou will be at peace and there will be no need for war..."

"He failed to do this when he was alive. Instead, he worked excessively, built palaces, and fought in the north and south. The world was exhausted, which led to a catastrophe. But now it's better. I have unified the nine states again, and the six kingdoms have been wiped out. Guandong is stable, and even the hidden dangers on the border, the Xiongnu, have fled north. The garrison soldiers traveling all over the world can go home. The farmers only need to pay ten percent of the rent. It can be regarded as men enjoying their fields and women cultivating their own industries. Orderly fun.”

Heifu spread his hands and said with a smile: "I will inherit this legacy!"

"Looking at it this way, whether we go east, west, or stay in the Central Plains, we are all the successors of the First Emperor!"

Xi sighed and said:

"The ambition you have inherited is the most difficult to achieve. Forty-eight counties, more than 20 million people, and people from the six countries that are difficult to reconcile are not comparable to Li Xin and Gongsun Jun who only have to be responsible for thousands of people. .”

"Is it difficult?" Xi asked Heifu. At this moment, he became the elder from the same hometown who taught Heifu dutifully.

"Disaster."

Heifu was stunned for a moment, then nodded with emotion: "Only when you really shoulder the heavy responsibility will you realize that starting a business is difficult, and keeping it is even harder."

He then avoided the banquet and bowed for a long time:

"Xi Jun, in addition to these three points, the First Emperor also has a legacy that has not yet been realized!"

"That is the method of Chu Ping, to review the duties and establish permanence."

"The great sage governs, establishes laws and regulations, and shows the rules and regulations!"

"Let Qin's laws and decrees be adapted to local conditions and truly spread throughout the world as a guideline for all generations!"

Xi remained silent and simply said: "Is this really the last wish of the First Emperor?"

Wasn't this how he persuaded Qin Shi Huang not to take the lead in breaking laws and regulations for his own selfish desires, so he was angered and moved away?

Heifu said: "Whether he is sincere or bragging, since he has made a promise, as a successor, he must fulfill it. I hope that one day, this world can truly rule the country according to law."

"Even if we exhaust the efforts of a generation, we can only make a small step toward that goal!"

"But if you want to do this, you can't rely on me alone, and you can't rely on the heroes of the dynasty who only care about the wealth of their descendants."

After the world is settled, the heroes have become the targets that Heifu must be wary of. This group of guys who have achieved a class leap will become corrupt very quickly.

Therefore, a truly fair person needs to stand up and rebuild the judicial system.

"If there is anyone in this world who can be fair and impartial and can enforce the law impartially, it must be Xijun!"

"If there is anyone in this world who can supervise me, it must be Xijun!"

"So, Xijun, you must be involved in this matter."

Hei Fu bowed with a long bow, just like Liu Bei inviting Zhuge Liang to come out:

"I would like to invite you to serve as the royal censor of the imperial court! Supervise the officials of the world, including me as the regent! And re-examine the laws and regulations, correct the shortcomings of the laws and regulations of the first emperor, and make Qin's laws and regulations enforceable in the world again."

"Let this world, where laws and rituals have collapsed, once again have the world's rules!"

Xi was a little moved, but did not agree to Heifu.

There was no rejection either.

Xi's eyes were sharp and he looked at Heifu steadily: "Like Li Xin, I also have a problem."

Just like Ling Shi's trial, no matter what the case is, no matter what the subjective judgment is, no matter what the objective evidence is, the suspect must be questioned according to the established procedures.

He was only asking the black husband, but he seemed to be asking all living beings, future generations, all the people who had read this story from the beginning to the end!

The happy question seems to span time and space, even penetrating the thin paper!

"Hei Fu, are you still a Qin official?"

…

ps: After thinking about it carefully, let’s put Li Xin’s story in a side story (well, if there is one).

Therefore, I will take my time on the 21st, and so will you. The last chapter on the 22nd will be the finale.
